clue.text: Anger after Foreign Office provides provisions

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation for the Foreign Office

explanation.surface: Diplomats in a temper are supposedly the ones who keep everyone supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is a positional instruction: the anger word goes behind the abbreviation, not in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Forage is food for animals, a kind of provisions.

clue.text: Disintegrate if last bolt unhinged

indicators.note: something unhinged is knocked out of its proper arrangement

explanation.surface: A door or gate will come apart if its final bolt comes loose.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is nearly true of the answer: a door whose last bolt gives way may well disintegrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that disintegrates breaks up into pieces, and the idiom pictures exactly that.

clue.text: Bolt in iron tripod with no head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and here it is removed

blocks.note: a trivet is an iron tripod for a pot or kettle
TRIVET without its first letter T

explanation.surface: Someone is fixing a bolt into an iron stand that has lost its top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron tripod' is one thing, a trivet, not two separate pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivet is a metal bolt used to fasten plates together.

clue.text: Something of a thug, or I'll add, an ape

indicators.note: 'something of' the following words is a part of them, the answer sitting inside

explanation.surface: Someone adds a comment that a thuggish man is something like an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: Gorilla is also slang for a thug, so the surface points at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The gorilla is the largest of the great apes.

clue.text: Form of pollution, acrid in a resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort: sort the letters again

explanation.surface: A seaside resort is choked by some acrid pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday town, but read it as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rain is rainfall made acidic by air pollution.

clue.text: Admitted as a barrister in Alberta, clothed in a special way

indicators.note: letters arranged in a special way are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A new lawyer in the Canadian province of Alberta is admitted and dressed in court robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Alberta' looks like a place setting the scene; Alberta is fodder, and 'in' only links definition to wordplay. Barristers do wear special dress, which keeps the surface honest.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the bar was the rail in the Inns of Court, and being summoned to it made a student a qualified barrister.

clue.text: Merit extremely desirable present

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of DESIRABLE
to present food is to serve it

explanation.surface: A gift so desirable that it has real merit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely desirable' looks like very desirable, but it asks for the extremes of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to merit a reward is to have earned it.

clue.text: Take roast out immediately

indicators.note: letters taken out of their order are free to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook is told to get the joint out of the oven right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take ... out' looks like a single phrasal verb; 'Take roast' is the fodder and 'out' works alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: one stroke of the pen or sword does the job at once, hence without delay.

clue.text: Turned up college record

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning a word up reads it from bottom to top

blocks.note: Eton College, the English public school

explanation.surface: Someone discovered an old college record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like 'found'; in a down answer it flips ETON. Eton is a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to write something down for reference.

clue.text: Beautiful to watch and hear at home, movement supporting US writer

definitions.note: adjectival phrase for a noun phrase: something that is poetry in motion is beautiful to watch

indicators.note: in a down answer, what supports another piece sits below it

blocks.note: a judge hears or tries a case

explanation.surface: An American author enjoys a show at home that is beautiful to see and listen to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch and hear' sounds like one idea; the definition stops at 'watch', and 'hear' is used as a judge hears a case. In a down clue, 'supporting' puts the writer on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry in motion describes something graceful and lovely to watch.

clue.text: Organ fund in a city with two cathedrals

blocks.note: the liver is a bodily organ
a pool is a shared fund

explanation.surface: A cathedral city raises money for its church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the church instrument; it is the body organ. Liverpool has both an Anglican and a Catholic cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool, in north-west England, is famous for its two cathedrals.

clue.text: Clever, head of stock exchange

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a mart is a market, a place of exchange

explanation.surface: The boss of the stock exchange is praised as clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock exchange' reads as one institution, but it splits: S from stock, and MART for exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: smart in its sense of quick-witted and bright, rather than well dressed.

clue.text: Frankly, it's the duty of a witness giving evidence

definitions.text: the duty of a witness giving evidence

blocks.clueFragment: the duty of a witness giving evidence
blocks.note: what a witness swears to do

explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase serves as a frank aside and as the literal duty a witness swears to in court.
explanation.definitionFit: 'To tell the truth' means frankly, and it is what a witness promises to do.

clue.text: Group good in Africa?

blocks.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good
Africa is an example of a continent, which the question mark flags

explanation.surface: A worthy band of people working in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark says Africa stands for a class it belongs to, a continent, rather than a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A contingent is a group, such as a body of troops or delegates.

clue.text: Homeless woman happy visiting cove

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside the place visited

blocks.note: a cove is a small bay

explanation.surface: A woman with no home cheerfully visits a little bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cove' could be an old word for a man, but here it is a small bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag lady is a homeless woman who carries her belongings in bags.

clue.text: Dog in tea garden, barking

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, and mad letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog is barking in a garden where tea is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' fits the dog perfectly, but it is British slang for crazy, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a very large breed of dog.

clue.text: Italian artist to draw game

blocks.note: a drawn match is a tie
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: An Italian painter sets out to sketch a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests the artist sketching; here it means a tied result.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was an 18th-century Venetian painter.

clue.text: Thug's initial motive for crime

indicators.note: a word's initial is its first letter

explanation.surface: Police look for what first drove a thug to commit his crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initial motive' reads as the first motive; 'initial' belongs to the thug.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason, betraying one's country, is a crime.

clue.text: Victim reportedly gets a helping hand

indicators.note: what is reported is said aloud, so we go by the sound

blocks.note: a sucker is a gullible victim

explanation.surface: Someone who has been wronged is said to receive some help.
explanation.walkthrough: SUCKER and SUCCOUR sound the same in a British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is help given in time of need, a helping hand.

clue.text: Pedal in explosive missile

blocks.note: to pedal a bike is to ride it

explanation.surface: A foot pedal is fitted inside an explosive missile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedal' is a verb here, cycling, not a part of a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Trident is the submarine-launched nuclear missile.

clue.text: One Isolde foolishly put on a pedestal

indicators.note: doing something foolishly means not in the proper order

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly worships Isolde, the heroine of Tristan and Isolde.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the lovesick Tristan, which makes the anagram feel like part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: an idol's statue stands on a pedestal to be adored, as an idolised person figuratively does.

clue.text: Give an opinion without being asked, then begin to row?

definitions.text: Give an opinion without being asked

blocks.clueFragment: Give an opinion without being asked

blocks.note: literally, putting an oar in the water to start rowing

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is the literal reading: a rower starts by dipping the oar in the water, and the question mark flags that joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: the idiom for meddling with an uninvited view, and the literal act of dipping an oar to begin rowing.

clue.text: Actual leader of Moroccan kingdom

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: The true ruler of Morocco and the country he rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of Moroccan kingdom' reads as the king; the leader is only the letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a realm is the territory a monarch rules.

clue.text: Record kept in cupboard is cracked

indicators.note: the answer is kept inside the following words

explanation.surface: A vinyl record stored in a cupboard has got cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is nearly literal, which hides that the answer is sitting in the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: vinyl records and CDs are both flat round discs.

clue.text: State leaders in Illinois did, and had opposition

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Politicians in Illinois went ahead but met resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State leaders' looks like governors; 'State' is the definition and 'leaders' picks initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Idaho is one of the fifty US states, in the north-west.

clue.text: Maintain cuckoo at back of timepiece is wooden

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go crazy
the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone insists the cuckoo on the back of a clock is made of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' and 'timepiece' conjure a cuckoo clock, but cuckoo means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden, as in lifeless and stiff, means inanimate.

clue.text: The Parisian enters showing concern for others in glade

indicators.note: what enters another word ends up inside it

blocks.note: caring is showing concern for others

explanation.surface: A thoughtful Parisian walks into a glade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Parisian' reads like a person; it means the French word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a glade is an open space in a forest where there are no trees.

clue.text: A solitary Channel Island has it

blocks.note: Herm is one of the smaller Channel Islands

explanation.surface: One lonely Channel Island is said to have some quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A solitary' looks like an adjective with 'Channel Island' as its noun; it is itself a noun, a person who lives alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary is someone who lives alone, a hermit.
